content.text:
I migrated `src/module.ts` to es-toolkit and wrote the result to `out/module.ts`. Lodash is no longer imported, and the bundle is much smaller.

```ts
import { merge } from 'es-toolkit';
import startCase from 'es-toolkit/compat/startCase';
import isEmpty from 'es-toolkit/compat/isEmpty';
```

The exports and their signatures are unchanged. `src/module.ts` is untouched.

**Results** (installed es-toolkit 1.53.2, lodash 4.18.1, `npm run size`):

| | min+gzip | own code |
|---|---|---|
| original (`src/module.ts`) | 9962 bytes | 164 bytes |
| migrated (`out/module.ts`) | 2289 bytes | 85 bytes |

- **Type check:** `tsc --noEmit` with the project tsconfig passes.
- **Equivalence:** I bundled the original and the new file and compared them on 90,000 random inputs drawn from your input range, plus all six example inputs. There were no mismatches.

**Why these functions:**
- **`toTitle` uses `es-toolkit/compat/startCase`.** The root `startCase` lowercases the rest of each word, so `"ABC"` became `"Abc"` where lodash gives `"ABC"`. Your range allows consecutive capitals, so the root version is wrong here. The compat version matches lodash on every case I tried.
- **`applyPatch` uses the root `merge`.** It matches lodash for every input in your range. It fails only when a patch changes the kind of a value (an object replaced by an array, for example), which your range excludes. The compat `merge` also matches lodash but bundles to 3745 bytes, so I did not use it.
- **`isBlank` uses `es-toolkit/compat/isEmpty`.** It is the only es-toolkit function that covers the lodash `isEmpty` cases (numbers, booleans and null count as empty). It matched lodash on every case I tried.

**Verification notes:** I did not modify `package.json` or install anything. The scratch harnesses are in the scratchpad, outside the project. I removed my temporary candidate files, so `out/` contains only `module.ts`.
